text:
maya: quick thought — our dash renders are still sensitive to auth checks inside the query path. what if we extract a tiny prefilter that only returns tenant+perm bitsets and do full policy evaluation async? :thinking:

sam: i like the idea of moving the hot path to a smaller RPC. what latency target are we aiming for on the dash's critical render?

maya: current median auth add is ~45ms on p95 requests when the query fanout is large. goal is to get that median auth impact under 15ms for common paths (single-tenant dashboards). rough win: 20–30ms.

liam: concern: splitting auth changes the failure modes. if prefilter is stale we might under-apply permissions and expose data. how do we keep it correct?

maya: two parts — strong cache invalidation on write path + conservative fallthrough. prefilter returns a conservative allow-mask. UI still double-checks for risky actions server-side. basically: fast-pass for read-only panels, strict server check for writes.

carla: ops implication — another RPC endpoint to maintain. what's the throughput? can we batch checks?

dinesh: batching looks feasible. policy prefilter can accept an array of subject+resource and return compact bitsets. bandwidth cheap, CPU cheap. sketch: 
```
POST /v1/auth/prefilter
body: { checks: [{subject: "u:123", resource: "dash:456"}, ...] }
resp: { results: ["0x4", "0x0", "0x6"] }
```

sam: how do we wire this in the dashboard service? option A: prefilter call from UI server before issuing queries. option B: prefilter in query gateway and attach mask to requests to downstream services.

maya: prefer B — keeps UI dumb and lets gateway attach masks to requests so downstream can short-circuit rendering. also easier to measure before/after.

liam: rollout plan: 1) implement prefilter service behind feature flag; 2) gateway uses it only for tenants with low fanout; 3) graduate after two weeks of telemetry. add a kill switch.

carla: telemetry to add: auth rpc latency histogram, mismatch alerts (prefilter vs full-check diffs), coverage of tenants on flag. also cost estimate: extra small fleet of CPUs vs saved GPU/query cost from reduced fanout.

dinesh: note on mismatch alerts — we should sample 1% of requests and run both prefilter+full-policy to detect divergence. ship a countermetric and an abstracted eval pipeline so we can flip to strict mode if divergence > 0.1%.

maya: ops-bot can we get a quick staging deploy after the prototype lands? want canary numbers on staging with a synthetic dash workload. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary for branch "prefilter-proto" queued to staging. expected finish ~30m.

sam: one more potential pitfall — multi-tenant dashboards that embed cross-tenant widgets. prefilter must understand seat-level scopes. recommendation: start with single-tenant-only path to lower blast radius.

maya: agreed. start small. i'll draft a short RFC with interfaces, rollout steps, metrics and the conservative fallback semantics. assign owners: maya (arch), liam (auth), carla (ops), dinesh (telemetry), sam (gateway integration).

liam: +1 on owners. quick nit: include how this interacts with existing tenant pinning and cache invalidation.

carla: will add maintenance playbook for the new endpoint (rotate keys, throttling, perf knobs).

maya: thanks all. i'll post the RFC link here when ready and we'll sync next Tue for design review.

sam: sounds good. excited to shave that latency down.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment finished — staging results: prefilter median 6ms, p95 18ms, full pipeline shows 22ms median auth time reduction for sampled dashboards. logs pushed to /staging/prefilter/run-20295.

dinesh: awesome numbers. i'll correlate with dashboard render times and post a short graph in the RFC.

maya: perfect. moving to draft RFC now. :rocket:
